name: node-fly
shape: Node.js (TypeScript) services in a Rush monorepo on Fly.io: an API and two timer loops on one machine, a Vite web app

platform.name: Fly.io
platform.why: fly.toml declares app govsky with an http_service on port 3000, auto_stop_machines off, and a release_command

processes.note: the Dockerfile's CMD runs this script, which starts projects/api (node dist/index.js) in the background on the same machine as the two loops below
projects/plc-backfill/index.ts: two setInterval loops, every 15 minutes each
projects/bots/index.ts: runBots at start and every 15 minutes by setInterval; the script's foreground process

data.note: Prisma datasource postgresql on DATABASE_URL; docker-compose.yml runs postgres:14.1-alpine for development only

notes: There is no Go in this repository: it is TypeScript built with Rush (rush.json lists api, plc-backfill, bots, database, config, web), so the shape in repos.txt is wrong. Read fly.toml, the Dockerfile, scripts/start_govsky_service.sh, docker-compose.yml, the workflow and every .ts file under projects/. One Fly machine runs three node processes; after a move the API is the web service and the two 15-minute setInterval loops become scheduled jobs. projects/api/cache.ts is a per-instance in-memory cache with a 5-minute expiry, not a session store, so it is not a finding. projects/web is a Vite React SPA that rush deploy can bundle, but nothing in the repository says where it is hosted; it is browser code with no rule pattern in it, and setTimeout delays in plc-backfill and bots are awaited inside their runs.

known.process missing: 2 x cron: two loops inside a shell script that the Dockerfile runs; a shell script is no manifest any reader opens
